subject: Near-term go-live: MAP slip detection & escalation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@medsprint.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Near-term go-live: MAP slip detection & escalation

Hi Emily —

Quick heads up from our side: during a routine run of the MAP acceptance checklist this morning we observed two procurement gating items that are unlikely to be cleared before your original 11/3 go-live target. Specifically: a third-party DPA signature and the PO confirmation for the dedicated capacity pool.

I attached an updated MAP (2025-10-20_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a one-page risk log (map-risk-log-20251021.csv) summarizing the impact and a short set of options (fast-track signatures, temporary burst, or a 2-week re-baseline).

Can you confirm whether MedSprint procurement has visibility on the PO timeline? If not, would you like us to loop in our procurement channel and offer a credit-backed burst to bridge the gap?

Short note at the top: we prefer to avoid a re-baseline but want to align now so there are no surprises. Proposed next step: 30-min call today or tomorrow to confirm actions and owners.

Thanks —
Jonas
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 2025-10-20_MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: map-risk-log-20251021.csv (CSV risk summary)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@medsprint.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSprint Procurement <procurement@medsprint.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Near-term go-live: MAP slip detection & escalation

Thanks for the heads up, Jonas.

I appreciate the clear summary and the updated MAP. Short context from procurement: the PO is pending legal review for the third-party DPA rider — we just received a redline request from our counsel this morning. Realistically, that pushes PO issuance 7–10 business days unless we expedite. I'll loop our procurement lead (cc'd) to coordinate.

We very much want to keep the 11/3 window if we can. Two asks from my side:
1) Can Redwood provide an interim technical support window (short-term extra capacity) in case we need to start verification before the PO clears?
2) If procurement cannot meet 11/3, what's your recommended minimum re-baseline to preserve milestone gating (staging sign-off, final eval window)?

I can do a 30-min call tomorrow at 11AM PT.

Emily Park
Sr. Product Ops Lead — MedSprint
emily.park@medsprint.com

Attachment: medsprint_internal_note.txt (procurement summary)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Oct 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Near-term go-live: MAP slip detection & escalation

Team —

I ran the acceptance gating matrix with Eng and Services. Short summary and recommendation attached (medsprint_procurement_timeline.pdf):
- Root cause: legal redline for DPA rider + procurement queue backlog for PO issuance. Current estimate: 7–10 business days to PO.
- Impact: blocks capacity reservation; staging can proceed but final sign-off dependent on production keys and PO.
- Short-term mitigations we can offer: 48–72 hour burst (credit-backed), remote-only verification environment, and a priority legal review template to speed counsel sign-off.

My recommendation (to give sales a customer-friendly option without stretching delivery):
1) Offer a one-week technical window (no prod tokens) + a capped credit for burst hours to enable early validation.
2) If procurement cannot commit to PO within 7 business days, propose a formal re-baseline to 11/17 to protect the acceptance window and preserve cutover readiness.
3) Escalate to the MedSprint exec sponsor only if procurement cannot commit by Fri 10/24 — that gives us time to exhaust mitigation.

I updated the risk log with quantified exposure and included an action list with owners. Please review and confirm before I send a customer-facing note.

Camila Reyes
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: medsprint_procurement_timeline.pdf (timeline & owners), map-risk-log-20251021.csv (updated risk exposures)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@medsprint.com>, MedSprint Procurement <procurement@medsprint.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Bcc: lauren@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Oct 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation & proposed mitigations for 11/3 readiness — immediate actions

Emily / Procurement team —

Following internal triage, we want to make the path to 11/3 as narrow as possible. To summarize our offer and ask:

Redwood offers (immediately):
- A 72-hour verification window in our pre-prod environment starting on your signal (no production tokens) with priority onboarding support.
- Up to 120 burst GPU hours, credit-backed (applied as a one-time invoice credit) to cover early testing and load checks.
- A legal playbook template for the DPA rider to reduce back-and-forth with counsel (attached).

We ask (MedSprint):
- Confirm by EOB Thu 10/23 whether procurement can commit to issuing the PO within 7 business days.
- If not, agree to re-baseline the go-live to 11/17 so we can preserve the final eval window without compressing staging sign-off.

If procurement needs, I will escalate to our CRO and request a credit exception beyond the 120 hours — but I want to avoid exec-level escalation unless the customer asks for it.

Next step: Emily — confirm availability for a 30-min alignment call tomorrow 11AM PT so we can lock owners and I can send a single customer-facing MAP addendum.

Best —
Jonas Weber
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Attachments: 2025-10-20_MAP_v2.xlsx (updated MAP), medsprint_procurement_timeline.pdf (timeline & owners), map-risk-log-20251021.csv (risk exposures)
